'''Friedrich E. Wagner''' (born November 16, 1943, sometimes abbreviated as Fritz Wagner) is a German physicist and [[Emeritus|emeritus professor]] who specializes in [[Plasma (physics)|plasma physics]]. He was known to have discovered the [[high-confinement mode]] (i.e. H-mode) of [[Magnetic confinement fusion|magnetic confinement]] in fusion plasmas while working at the [[ASDEX Upgrade|ASDEX tokamak]] in 1982.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Wagner|first1=F.|last2=Becker|first2=G.|last3=Behringer|first3=K.|last4=Campbell|first4=D.|last5=Eberhagen|first5=A.|last6=Engelhardt|first6=W.|last7=Fussmann|first7=G.|last8=Gehre|first8=O.|last9=Gernhardt|first9=J.|last10=Gierke|first10=G. v.|last11=Haas|first11=G.|date=1982|title=Regime of Improved Confinement and High Beta in Neutral-Beam-Heated Divertor Discharges of the ASDEX Tokamak|journal=Physical Review Letters|language=en|volume=49|issue=19|pages=1408–1412|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.49.1408|bibcode=1982PhRvL..49.1408W|issn=0031-9007}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=How Fritz Wagner 'discovered' the H-Mode|url=http://www.iter.org/newsline/86/659|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200419153827/https://www.iter.org/newsline/86/659|archive-date=2020-04-19|access-date=2020-06-13|website=ITER|language=en}}</ref> For this discovery and his subsequent contributions to fusion research, was awarded the [[John Dawson Award for Excellence in Plasma Physics Research|John Dawson Award]] in 1987, the [[Hannes Alfvén Prize]] in 2007 and the [[Stern–Gerlach Medal]] in 2009.

== Life and career ==
Wagner was born in [[Pfaffenhofen an der Roth]] in [[Bavaria, Germany]]. He studied at the [[Technical University of Munich]] and completed his doctorate in 1972. He then worked at [[Ohio State University]] from 1973 to 1974. At first, he worked on [[Low Temperature Physics|low-temperature physics]], but switched to [[Magnetic confinement fusion|plasma fusion]] research during the energy crisis of the time. In 1975, he started working for the [[Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics]], and in 1986 he led the tokamak experiment [[ASDEX Upgrade|ASDEX]].

In 1988, Wagner habilitated at [[Heidelberg University]] and was given a teaching position there. He was then appointed honorary professor at the [[Technical University of Munich]]. From 1989 to 1993, Wagner was project manager of the [[Wendelstein 7-AS]] stellarator experiment.

In 1993, he became the director of the [[Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics]] and was Chairman of the Plasma Physics Department of the [[European Physical Society]] between 1996 and 2004. In 1999, he became full professor at the [[Ernst Moritz Arndt University]] in Greifswald. From 2003 to 2005, he was head of the [[Wendelstein 7-X]] experiment. He retired in 2008.

He was President of the [[European Physical Society]] between 2007 and 2009.

== Honors and awards ==
Wagner is an honorary member of the [[Ioffe Institute]] at St. Petersburg and a fellow of the [[Institute of Physics]] and the [[American Physical Society]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Prof. Dr. Friedrich Wagner|url=https://www.ipp.mpg.de/1084906/wagner|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-06-13|website=www.ipp.mpg.de|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=APS Fellow Archive|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1991&unit_id=DPP&institution=Max+Planck+Institute|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-06-13|website=American Physical Society|language=en}}</ref>

In 1987, Wagner was awarded the [[John Dawson Award for Excellence in Plasma Physics Research]] from the [[American Physical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=1987 John Dawson Award for Excellence in Plasma Physics Research Recipient|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Wagner&first_nm=Fritz&year=1987|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-06-13|website=American Physical Society|language=en}}</ref>

In 2007, he received the [[Hannes Alfvén Prize]] from the [[European Physical Society]] for his contributions to fusion research by [[Magnetic confinement fusion|magnetic confinement]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Alfvén Prize {{!}} European Physical Society – Plasma Physics Division|url=http://plasma.ciemat.es/eps/awards/alfven-prize/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-06-13|website=European Physical Society|language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2009, he received the [[Stern–Gerlach Medal]], the highest honour for [[experimental physics]] awarded by the [[German Physical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Die Physik-Preisträger 2009|url=https://www.dpg-physik.de/veroeffentlichungen/aktuell/2008/dpg-pm-2008-025|access-date=2020-06-13|website=DPG|language=en}}</ref> He was awarded in honor of his work in high-temperature plasma physics and fusion research, especially for the discovery of self-organizing transport barriers (i.e. H-mode), which was groundbreaking for the mastery of fusion plasmas.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Smith|first1=Z E.|last2=Wagner|first2=S.|date=1987|title=Band Tails, Entropy, and Equilibrium Defects in Hydrogenated Amorphous Silicon|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=59|issue=15|pages=688–691|doi=10.1103/physrevlett.59.1790.3|pmid=10035845|issn=0031-9007|doi-access=free}}</ref>
